questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
In the diagram, JK is an economy’s production possibility curve. J G industrial goods O H K agricultural goods What could cause the curve to shift to GH?

options.A: a decrease in innovation
options.B: an increase in the retirement age
options.C: an increase in the price of energy
options.D: an increase in the unemployment rate

questions.questionText: What is the opportunity cost to a fully employed economy of increasing capital investment?

options.A: a fall in consumption
options.B: a fall in income
options.C: a rise in saving
options.D: a rise in the rate of interest

questions.questionText: Skilled actors deserve to receive a high income because they bring pleasure to people who attend the theatre. What can be concluded about this statement?

options.A: It is a normative statement because both services and goods are economic outputs.
options.B: It is a normative statement because it expresses an opinion.
options.C: It is a positive statement because actors do bring pleasure to people.
options.D: It is a positive statement because greater skill results in higher pay.

questions.questionText: What is a market demand curve?

options.A: the demand for all of a country’s products
options.B: the total sum of individual demand curves for a product
options.C: the output of all the firms in an industry
options.D: the stocks of a particular good available for sale

questions.questionText: A good has a unitary price elasticity of demand and at a price of $20 a firm sells 40 000 units. How many will the firm sell if it charges a price of $5?
The cross elasticity of demand between two products, X and Y, is negative. What would be the immediate effect of a rise in the price of product Y?

options.A: Quantity demanded of product X will fall.
options.B: Supply of product X will rise.
options.C: The cross elasticity of demand will rise.
options.D: The price of product X would rise.

The demand for a good falls at the same time as its costs of production decrease. What will be the combined effect of these changes on the price and on the quantity supplied of the good? price quantity supplied

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease uncertain
options.C: uncertain decrease
options.D: uncertain uncertain

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the effect of the imposition of a tax equal to FG on a commodity. S S price u x y v F w G D O quantity Which area represents the reduction in consumer surplus?

options.A: u + v B u + x C u + x + y D x + w

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the average world price of coffee in US cents per pound weight (lb) between 1997 and 2005. The price of coffee, 1997 to 2005 US cents/lb 75 1997 2001 2005 year Which event is consistent with the price behaviour shown in the specified time period?

options.A: a continuous rise in the price of tea between 1997 and 2001
options.B: the entry to the market of new producers of coffee between 1997 and 2001
options.C: a series of good coffee harvests between 2001 and 2005
options.D: increasing health worries about drinking coffee between 2001 and 2005

questions.questionText: What is not a function of the price mechanism?

options.A: to ensure that firms make profits
options.B: to permit consumers to express their preferences
options.C: to ration scarce resources
options.D: to signal where resources are required

questions.questionText: Which statement is correct?

options.A: External cost equals social cost minus private cost.
options.B: Private cost equals external cost minus social cost.
options.C: Social cost equals external cost minus private cost.
options.D: Social cost equals private cost minus external cost.

questions.questionText: In deciding whether to invest in a new project, what would be taken into account in government cost-benefit analysis but not by a private company?

options.A: consultancy fees
options.B: consumer surplus
options.C: interest charges
options.D: tax payments

questions.questionText: Why does the production of public goods have to be financed by the government?

options.A: One person’s consumption of a public good means it is not available for anyone else.
options.B: People are able to consume public goods without paying for them.
options.C: Private sector firms will charge a price significantly above cost for public goods.
options.D: The cost of producing public goods is higher in the private sector.

questions.questionText: The government has to choose the best one of four possible sites to locate a port. The benefits and costs of each site are shown in $m in the table. Which site would be chosen? private external private external benefits benefits costs costs
The diagram shows the market for spectacles. Initially the market equilibrium price is P and O quantity Q is bought and sold. S P X P price O P M D O Q Q Q Q Q
Thailand produces rubber at a lower opportunity cost than China. It does, however, import some rubber from China. What could explain Thailand importing rubber from China?

options.A: China imposes lower tariffs on rubber imports than Thailand.
options.B: China is consuming increasing quantities of rubber in industry.
options.C: Thailand has the absolute but not the comparative advantage in rubber production.
options.D: Thailand wants to avoid the risks involved in overspecialising in rubber production.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the production possibility curves for two countries, X and Y.

options.A: decrease in productivity moves country X’s production possibility curve from X to X .

questions.questionText: The diagram shows that the imposition of a tariff raises price from $10 to $14. domestic supply D price $ domestic demand S 0 20 30 70 100 quantity (millions) What is the value of tax revenue raised?

options.A: $80 million
options.B: $160 million
options.C: $320 million
options.D: $400 million

questions.questionText: A firm borrows money from a bank based abroad in order to pay a lower rate of interest than that available from banks in its own country. Which two parts of the balance of payments accounts will be affected by this transaction?

options.A: capital account and currency reserves
options.B: capital account and trade in services
options.C: financial account and net income flows
options.D: financial account and net current transfers

questions.questionText: The table gives unemployment rates (%) for four countries in 1993 and 2002. UK Japan France Italy 1993 10.5 2.5 11.4 10.1 2002 5.0 5.4 8.8 8.5 What can be deduced from the table?

options.A: France had the lowest rate of employment in both years.
options.B: Italy had the most employed people in 2002.
options.C: Japan more than doubled its labour productivity between 1993 and 2002.
options.D: The UK created the most jobs between 1993 and 2002.

questions.questionText: In which year did the real value of money rise? Price Index year (base year 2001)
A country experienced a significant fall in unemployment but its inflation rate remained low. What could explain this?

options.A: Global competition prevented firms passing on higher costs.
options.B: Increased spending on imports had lowered the exchange rate.
options.C: There was a low level of spare capacity in the economy.
options.D: Wage rates had increased by more than labour productivity.

questions.questionText: Before 1999 the Brazilian government did not have a desired target rate of inflation. From 1999 it set target rates within an upper and lower boundary. The diagram shows the rate of inflation between 1994 and 2003 and the target rate between 1999 and 2003. Inflation and inflation targets in Brazil, 1994 to 2003 % government target
A government decides to reduce the quota on imported cars from 2000 to 1000 per year. What is likely to happen?

options.A: The balance of trade may improve.
options.B: The demand for the good will increase.
options.C: The good will become cheaper.
options.D: The government’s revenue will decline.

questions.questionText: A representative basket of goods costs $2500 in the United States. The same basket of goods costs £2000 in the UK. What can be deduced from this?

options.A: The £ sterling is 25% overvalued.
options.B: The £ sterling is 20% undervalued.
options.C: The purchasing power parity exchange rate of the £ sterling is $0.80 to the £.
options.D: The purchasing power parity exchange rate of the £ sterling is $1.25 to the £.

questions.questionText: The price of a good traded internationally increases. Who would be disadvantaged the most?

options.A: high income countries that pursue a policy of self sufficiency
options.B: high income countries with a balance of payments surplus that export the good
options.C: low income countries dependent on importing the good
options.D: low income countries with alternative suppliers of the good

questions.questionText: A country has a deficit on the current account of its balance of payments. What might help the country to reduce its deficit?

options.A: a decrease in its rate of income tax
options.B: a decrease in its tariffs
options.C: an increase in its level of employment
